microtheory.name: color_vision
microtheory.definition: How color is sensed + represented. Cone photoreceptors, opponent processing, color spaces, color constancy. Substrate analogue: substrate's chromatic processing channel.

concepts.name: trichromacy
concepts.definition: Young + Helmholtz. Three cone types (S, M, L) tuned to short, medium, long wavelengths. Three channels capture full color gamut. Substrate analogue: substrate's three primary color channels.

concepts.name: cone_photoreceptor
concepts.definition: S (419nm peak, blue), M (530nm, green), L (560nm, red). Substrate analogue: substrate's wavelength-selective sensors.

concepts.name: metamer
concepts.definition: Different spectral compositions producing identical perceived color. Why three primaries suffice. Substrate analogue: substrate's many-to-one color mapping.

concepts.name: spectral_sensitivity
concepts.definition: Cone response curve vs wavelength. Substrate analogue: substrate's color-channel response curve.

concepts.name: opponent_process_theory
concepts.definition: Hering 1892. Three opponent channels: red-green, blue-yellow, black-white. Cannot perceive reddish-green or bluish-yellow. Substrate analogue: substrate's contrast-channel pairs.

concepts.name: color_opponency_neural
concepts.definition: LGN + V1 neurons compute opponent signals: (L-M), (S - (L+M)/2). Substrate analogue: substrate's chromatic-contrast computation.

concepts.name: color_afterimage
concepts.definition: Stare at red, see green afterimage. Opponent channel adaptation. Substrate analogue: substrate's opponent-channel hysteresis.

concepts.name: hue
concepts.definition: The color name dimension. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet. Circular. Substrate analogue: substrate's chromatic-angle.

concepts.name: saturation
concepts.definition: Color purity / intensity. From gray (zero) to spectral (maximum). Substrate analogue: substrate's chromatic-magnitude.

concepts.name: brightness
concepts.definition: Perceived luminance. Substrate analogue: substrate's luminance channel.

concepts.name: color_space
concepts.definition: Coordinate system for representing colors. RGB, HSV, CIE Lab, XYZ. Different ones for different purposes. Substrate analogue: substrate's color-coordinate representations.

concepts.name: rgb_color_space
concepts.definition: Red, green, blue additive primaries. Used in displays. Substrate analogue: substrate's display color encoding.

concepts.name: cmyk_color_space
concepts.definition: Cyan, magenta, yellow, key (black) subtractive. Used in print. Substrate analogue: substrate's reflective-medium color.

concepts.name: hsv_color_space
concepts.definition: Hue, saturation, value. Perceptually-organized. Used in selection interfaces. Substrate analogue: substrate's perceptual color organization.

concepts.name: cie_lab
concepts.definition: Perceptually uniform color space. L = lightness, a/b = chromatic axes. Substrate analogue: substrate's perceptually-uniform color encoding.

concepts.name: color_constancy
concepts.definition: Same object appears similar color under different illumination. Retinex theory (Land). Brain discounts illumination. Substrate analogue: substrate's illumination-invariant color.

concepts.name: retinex_theory
concepts.definition: Land 1964. Color depends on spatial comparison across image. Substrate analogue: substrate's contextual color computation.

concepts.name: lightness_constancy
concepts.definition: Same surface appears same lightness under different illumination. Substrate analogue: substrate's lightness-from-reflectance estimate.

concepts.name: color_deficiency
concepts.definition: Anomalous trichromacy (most common) + dichromacy (one cone missing) + monochromacy (rare). Protanopia (L), deuteranopia (M), tritanopia (S). Substrate analogue: substrate's per-instance sensor variation.

concepts.name: tetrachromacy
concepts.definition: Four cone types. Rare in humans (~2% women carriers); common in birds + reptiles. Substrate analogue: substrate's extended chromatic range.

concepts.name: color_naming_universals
concepts.definition: Berlin + Kay 1969. Cross-culturally, color terms emerge in fixed order: black/white → red → green/yellow → blue → brown → others. Substrate analogue: substrate's perceptual-category prior.

concepts.name: categorical_color_perception
concepts.definition: Boundaries between color categories sharper than within. Influenced by language. Substrate analogue: substrate's category-warped representation.

concepts.name: memory_color
concepts.definition: Stored color associations for familiar objects (yellow banana, red tomato). Bias actual perception. Substrate analogue: substrate's prior-biased color recognition.

concepts.name: color_for_object
concepts.definition: Color carries object identity info. Yellow → banana. Substrate analogue: substrate's color-Concept binding.

rules.name: trichromacy_reduces_spectrum_to_three_channels
rules.head: the substrate processes color input
rules.body: wavelength is reduced to three channels (S, M, L cone responses). Higher-dimensional spectral info is lost. Substrate's three-channel chromatic encoding.

rules.name: opponent_processing_organizes_color
rules.head: the substrate processes color past primary cones
rules.body: opponent channels (red-green, blue-yellow, black-white) emerge. Cannot perceive reddish-green. Substrate's opponent organization.

rules.name: color_constancy_via_spatial_comparison
rules.head: the substrate sees a colored object under varying illumination
rules.body: spatial comparison (Retinex) discounts illumination + preserves surface color identity. Substrate's illumination-invariant color.

rules.name: language_warps_color_categorization
rules.head: the substrate has learned color terms
rules.body: the categorical boundaries become sharper at named-color borders. Whorf effect. Substrate's language-warped categories.

rules.name: memory_color_biases_perception
rules.head: the substrate sees a familiar object
rules.body: its expected color (yellow banana) biases the percept toward the memorized hue. Substrate's prior-modulated perception.
